meta.title: CarrierBridge — Carrier rate sheet comparison
meta.description: Load your carriers' Excel rate sheets exactly as they arrive. CarrierBridge names the best price per shipment and checks fuel indexation on your invoices.

hero.subtitle: Import every rate sheet, whatever the format. CarrierBridge names the best carrier for each shipment and checks that surcharges and fuel indexation do not drift. No TMS, no dedicated transport buyer.

Fuel indexation gaps flagged, not discovered at year end

problem.h2: Why do shippers award to only two or three carriers?
problem.lede: Because beyond that, tracking them in spreadsheets stops working. The ceiling is not commercial, it is practical: nobody can compare fifteen rate sheets in fifteen formats on every shipment. So you lose twice — at tender, for want of competition, and day to day, for want of arbitration on each order.

items.title: Rate sheets that cannot be compared
items.text: Every carrier has its own format: different weight brackets, in-house zones, départements grouped another way. The same consignment does not read the same way from one sheet to the next. Your comparison workbook is wrong the moment one rate changes.

items.title: Opaque ancillary charges
items.text: The quoted price is never the price paid. Tail lift, booked delivery slots, dangerous goods, sheeting, waiting time, tolls: these lines follow rules specific to each carrier, and almost never make it into the comparison.

items.title: Fuel indexation nobody checks
items.text: The formula is signed at the start of the contract, then nobody recalculates it. The gap between what was agreed and what is invoiced settles in month after month, with nothing to flag it.

problem.consequence: So the saving won at tender evaporates during the year, while the order-management team spends its days hunting for a rate across fifteen files and calling sales reps to have it confirmed.

import.h2: How do you load a carrier rate sheet from Excel?
import.lede: You upload the file exactly as the carrier sent it. A conversational agent opens it on screen with you, shows what it has understood and asks you to decide wherever it is ambiguous. A few exchanges and the rate sheet is live. Nothing is retyped, nothing is reformatted.
import.formatsNote: CarrierBridge reads Excel files today. Rate sheets received as PDFs or scans are not processed yet.

items.title: An agent that reads the sheet with you
items.text: It displays the file, highlights what it has identified — headers, destinations, brackets, prices — and asks a question wherever two readings are possible. You answer in plain language, not in settings.

items.title: Files as they are, including the worst
items.text: Merged cells, several tables on one sheet, a column covering two carriers, prices carrying a comment, one tab per departure site, terms and conditions slipped in under the prices. That is the everyday reality: the file does not have to be tidied up first.

items.title: The carrier's own structure is kept
items.text: A town-by-carrier matrix, a scale by pallet count, a flat rate per trip, weight brackets by département: each sheet is loaded in its own logic. Nothing is forced into a house format — that is exactly what would destroy the information.

items.title: Ancillary terms captured with it
items.text: Empty pallet returns, waiting beyond an hour, site-access surcharges, the reference period for fuel indexation: the lines trailing at the bottom of the sheet follow the carrier instead of getting lost.

items.title: Rate sheet updates
items.text: A new version replaces the old one without starting over. Earlier versions stay available, so you can tell which rate applied on which date.

surcharges.h2: What do a carrier's ancillary charges actually contain?
surcharges.lede: The costs that almost never enter the comparison, and that make the difference between two apparently identical offers.

items.title: Fuel surcharge
items.text: Applied as a percentage of the base price, following a formula and an index specific to each contract.

items.title: Booked delivery slot
items.text: Charged whenever a delivery is made to an appointment. The amount and the trigger conditions vary widely between carriers.

items.title: Tail lift
items.text: At collection, at delivery, or both. Sometimes included up to a certain weight, often with a minimum charge.

items.title: Dangerous goods (ADR)
items.text: A percentage uplift or a flat fee per consignment, depending on the class and the quantities carried.

items.title: Empty pallet returns
items.text: Charged per pallet, at rates that vary twofold from one carrier to the next.

items.title: Site delivery surcharge
items.text: Delivery to a building site or a difficult access point, charged as a flat fee per call.

items.title: Sheeting and unsheeting
items.text: Charged per operation, with minimum-charge rules that differ from one carrier to the next.

items.title: Tolls and taxes
items.text: Passed on as a percentage of the price or per kilometre, depending on the roads used.

items.title: Waiting time
items.text: Beyond a free allowance at loading or delivery, charged in hourly blocks.

surcharges.conclusion: For a given shipment, CarrierBridge applies each carrier's own rules and shows the complete price, not just the base rate.

fuel.h2: How do you check fuel indexation on a transport invoice?
fuel.lede: You enter your contract formula and reference index once. CarrierBridge recalculates the expected surcharge for each period and compares it with what you were invoiced.

steps.title: Your formula, exactly as the contract states it
steps.text: Fuel share, reference index, base index, revision frequency. The formula stays yours: CarrierBridge neither imposes nor assumes one.

steps.title: Recalculated from published indices
steps.text: For each period the theoretical surcharge is recalculated from the matching index, then applied to the base price of your shipments.

steps.title: The gap, if there is one
steps.text: The difference between the invoiced rate and the expected rate is shown in points and converted into euros, carrier by carrier and month by month.

fuel.disclaimer: CarrierBridge flags a calculation gap. It does not read your contract and is no substitute for reading it or for legal advice. A flagged gap is a point to raise with your carrier, not a conclusion.
fuel.toolTeaser: An invoice to check right now? The indexation calculator is open to everyone, no sign-up.

bestPrice.h2: Which carrier is cheapest for this shipment?
bestPrice.lede: Weight, destination, services required. The full ranking appears in seconds, all charges included.

items.title: Each rate sheet queried in its own logic
items.text: For the same shipment, one reads by pallet count, another by destination town, a third by weight bracket per département. The conversion happens when the quote is produced, not at load time — doing it the other way round would throw away what makes each sheet worth having.

items.title: The complete price, not the base rate
items.text: Base rate, fuel surcharge for the period, ancillary charges requested: the figure shown is the one you will pay.

items.title: The gap made visible
items.text: Second and third place appear with their gap to the best price. When availability matters more than cost, you know exactly what that choice costs.

items.title: No hunting through files
items.text: No sorting through fifteen workbooks, no calling a sales rep to confirm a rate, no doubt about which version of the sheet is in force.

operations.h2: How do you assign transport orders without a TMS?
operations.lede: Day-to-day operations, from the internal request to the assignment, in one place.

items.title: Transport requests
items.text: Sites and departments file their need through a single form instead of by email. Nothing gets lost in an inbox.

items.title: Order aggregation
items.text: Shipments going to the same area on the same day are grouped before arbitration, which often tips the calculation towards a different carrier.

items.title: Assignment
items.text: The chosen carrier is named for each order, with a record of the decision and of the price at the time it was made.

items.title: Spot rates outside the sheets
items.text: When no rate sheet covers the need, the price negotiated for that job is captured and kept. Your one-off charters stop escaping the record.

registry.h2: How do you keep track of your carriers' compliance certificates?
registry.lede: One register for your carriers and the documents you ask them for.

items.title: Carrier record
items.text: Contacts, geographic coverage, vehicle types, rate sheets in force and their version history.

items.title: Compliance documents
items.text: Social security compliance certificate, transport licence, goods-in-transit insurance, bank details. Each document carries its expiry date.

items.title: Expiry flagged in advance
items.text: Documents approaching expiry are flagged before the date, not once they have lapsed.

registry.disclaimer: CarrierBridge centralises the documents you collect and alerts you to their expiry dates. It does not replace your own verification obligations and does not certify that a document is valid.

sourcing.badge: Beta — included in Pro and Business
sourcing.h2: How do you find new carriers?
sourcing.text: Describe what you need in plain language: a lane, a vehicle type, a particular constraint. The module suggests carriers that may fit, for you to approach at your next tender.
sourcing.caveat: This module is in beta. It is not charged separately and is not needed to use CarrierBridge: most of the value comes from the rate sheets you already have.

pricingTeaser.lede: Public prices, no negotiation required. You start free and move up when your volumes justify it.

support.h2: Do you need onboarding to get started?
support.lede: No. Signing up asks for no configuration and leads to a usable result in under ten minutes. Onboarding exists for teams that want to move faster, or go further.
support.tagline: For teams that want someone who knows both the transport trade and the tool.

finalCta.h2: Start with your own rate sheets
finalCta.text: Upload two or three files, enter a typical shipment, compare. Ten minutes will tell you whether the tool is worth anything to you — no card, no sales call.
